title: Match over an unboxed record takes the wrong case
summary: A match whose or-pattern is made of unboxed record patterns takes a case without testing another component of the scrutinee, with no warning. With a variant in place of the boolean the code reads the argument of a constant constructor (segmentation fault); `#()` and `#true | #false` patterns do the same.
cause: `typing/parmatch.ml`, `lub`, has no case for two unboxed record patterns (nor for `#()` or `#true`/`#false`), so the context of the or-pattern's handler loses a row and `lambda/matching.ml` leaves out a test.

fix.text: Adds the missing cases to `lub`. Builds; `test.ml` then prints the expected result; testsuite unchanged.

reference: related: PR #7450 (merged) mended the same fault in Parmatch.Compat.compat; a review comment there says lub has it too
